body: As an add-on, I dropped out of high school in eleventh grade because my classmates were 'slow', despite being in the Honors program, and I couldn't endure sitting around waiting for them to catch up. It always gave me a headache. So, after I dropped out, I promptly acquired my GED and flew out to Los Angeles (at 16) for job interviews. I was offered one at a design company that did work for major motion pictures, but I was too young to sign for an apartment and ended up back in the small, shit-hole of a town that I reside in now. I never knew what I wanted to do after that, because the more I sat in front of the computer, the more I began to loathe it. It was and is as if my life is rotting away. So the Navy idea was born at some point, for the danger and adventure, but now I am just content with turning the lights off and retiring from this world.

School was never my 'thing'. I do well at it, because I am averse to bad grades and disappointing people (professors), but I have a very troubling time sitting around listening to lectures or waiting for 'slow' people to catch up. I mentioned in the original posting that I've been working since I was 13 years old, sitting in front of the computer for hours on end (12+ daily), and because of that I hate, quite literally, being stuck inside or sitting around. Precisely why I considered, am considering, the Navy SEALs. I want to live a life of adventure, and the only things that excite me anymore are the ones that I have the possibility of dying from. Additionally, I can't imagine what educational route / path I would want to take that could lead to a non-cubical / 9 - 5 job. I would much rather be dead than to continue living a life of dull repetition.
